inspection_scope: Independent-variant review of t01 and t02 in captioned and caption-free renders at 360×640. Inspected all 13 consecutive native frames in each declared contact window, plus ordered shot samples and painted pixel-change observations. Gold was used behaviorally, not for pixel matching.

gates.evidence: In both shots, Bot’s tilted head, narrowed eyes, stable stance, and extended arm read as focused inspection at native mobile size.
t01 maintains the hand-to-paper grip throughout frames 24–36. In t02, the paper abruptly detaches from the hand at frames 91–93 (3.033–3.100s), travels independently, then snaps back by frame 94.

t01 develops from a lower to raised paper and retains restrained residual movement. t02’s dominant action is interrupted by an unmotivated paper displacement and snapback immediately after contact, so the energy does not describe a coherent lift-and-inspect action.

Both variants use a generic rectangular card with minimal paper-specific contour or surface character as the declared hero. The actual wall, floor, paper, and plant treatment also lacks the distinctive material separation and physical layering demonstrated by the retrieved gold.

Both variants repeat the same small Bot-and-rectangle arrangement in the lower portion of a largely empty field. Although wall, floor, and plant cues exist, the staging conflicts with the contract’s explicit warning against a generic rectangle, tiny Bot, and empty field.
Without captions, the raised source paper, Bot’s contacting hand, and inspection posture remain legible at the supplied 360×640 native resolution.

violations.observation: The declared hero is a nearly regular cream rectangle with only text lines, slight rotation, and a small shadow; it lacks a distinctive paper silhouette, surface identity, or convincing layered edge treatment.
violations.smallest_correction: Add one restrained paper-specific contour/material cue—such as a curled corner, folded edge, or layered sheet thickness—while preserving the existing palette and label.

violations.observation: The Bot and paper occupy a small lower action cluster beneath a very large undifferentiated wall area, reproducing the prohibited tiny-Bot/generic-rectangle/empty-field pattern.
violations.smallest_correction: Reframe the existing Bot-paper cluster larger and higher so the inspection relationship commands the frame; retain the plant and floor as subordinate cues.

violations.observation: As in t01, the hero remains a generic rectangular card without the distinctive silhouette, material identity, and physical layering required of a hero object.
violations.smallest_correction: Give the paper a restrained irregular edge, fold, or layered thickness that remains readable at 360×640.

violations.observation: The second independent variant repeats the small lower cluster and broad empty wall, leaving the declared focal paper visually underweighted.
violations.smallest_correction: Increase and elevate the Bot-paper action cluster within the frame while keeping the plant secondary.

violations.observation: On frame 91, immediately after declared contact, the paper separates from Bot’s hand and jumps toward the right edge; it remains detached through frames 92–93 before snapping back at frame 94.
violations.smallest_correction: Keep the paper’s left-edge grip anchor resolved to the raised hand on every frame 91–94, applying any paper reaction around that anchored point.

violations.observation: The post-contact paper excursion and snapback are not a bounded local reaction or inspection gesture; they interrupt the dominant action with an unmotivated teleport-like beat.
violations.smallest_correction: Replace the detached excursion with a small anchored paper flex or rotational settle that decays locally while Bot continues inspecting.

sampling_limits: Assessment is limited to supplied decoded native images, consecutive contact windows, ordered sparse samples, and non-semantic pixel-change traces. No MP4 playback or audio listening was performed. Pixel deltas alone were not treated as proof of motion; behavior outside the supplied consecutive windows can only be inferred from ordered stills.

gates.evidence: Focused face, head tilt, extended arm, and grounded stance clearly support inspection.
The hand remains attached to the paper edge across every supplied consecutive frame 24–36, with no visible grip break.
Ordered samples show the paper rising from its lower state into the held state, followed by restrained residual change rather than an unsupported long dead hold.
The hero paper remains a generic rectangle without distinctive contour, material character, or layered construction.
The focal cluster is small and low, while most of the frame is an undifferentiated empty wall.
The paper, contacting hand, and focused inspection pose remain understandable without captions at native size.
Bot’s focused facial geometry, tilt, and raised-arm silhouette read clearly at native size.
Frames 91–93 show a clear hand-paper detachment and independent paper travel before reattachment at frame 94.
The paper’s abrupt detached excursion and snapback undermine the intended coherent lift-and-inspect action.
The hero repeats the same generic rectangular construction with insufficient paper-specific silhouette and layering.
The small lower action cluster and dominant empty wall leave the hero underweighted.
Outside the brief physicality defect, the core paper-inspection relationship remains readable without captions at 360×640.
